newsitem.title: CROATIA: Polls open in Croatia's presidential election.
newsitem.headline: Polls open in Croatia's presidential election.

text.p: Polling stations across Croatia opened on Sunday in the former Yugoslav republic's second presidential election since the fall of communism, which the incumbent Franjo Tudjman is expected to win.
Just over four million voters, including 377,705 living outside the country, are qualified to cast their ballots in 7,558 polling stations, including 199 abroad.
Polling stations in Croatia opened at 7 a.m. on an exceptionally clear and warm Sunday morning and are to be closed 12 hours later.
Voters in the last Serb-controlled area of Eastern Slavonia, due to revert to Croatian rule in a month, are also eligible.
Some 150 delegates of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) will monitor the poll.
First unofficial results are expected around midnight.
Croatia's 75-year old president Tudjman is running for his second five-year term in office despite reports that he is suffering from stomach cancer.

Tudjman's opponents, Social Liberal Vlado Gotovac who stands for nine centrist parties, and Social Democrat (former communist) Zdravko Tomac, would be satisfied if they force Tudjman him the second round.
If none of the candidates wins over 50 percent of votes, the two top-placed ones compete again on June 29.

But that seems unlikely as polls show that Tudjman, the self-styled "Father of the Nation" who steered the country to independence from former Yugoslavia and the 1991-95 war, still enjoys enormous popularity.
The election campaign was marred by a series of incidents in which both opposition candidates' vans were stoned, and one in which Gotovac was attacked by a Croatian army captain during a rally.
Gotovac sustained concussion and, after spending two days in hospital, was forced to cut down on campaign activities. The government rejected demands that the poll be postponed because of the attack.
